title: Fix NUMERIC columns being converted to integers (#624)
description:

- Ensure bigint conversion only applies to true INTEGER columns
- Add comprehensive test case to prevent regression

title: Fix POSIXt precision and tzone
description:
Two steps here for `POSIXt` value preservation:

- sets `"tzone"` attribute when missing/empty
- add `options(bigrquery.digits.secs=6)` to allow sending up to 6 sub-second digits to `POSIXt`-class objects

Before this patch,

```r
bq_auth(path="my_token.json")
tbl <- data.frame(dbl=pi, psx=Sys.time())
ds <- bigrquery::bq_table(...)
bq_table_upload(ds, tbl); tbl2 <- bq_table_download(ds); bq_table_delete(ds)
tbl$psx - tbl2$psx
# Time difference of 5.000016 hours
```

Just fixing "tzone", we can get

```r
bq_table_upload(ds, tbl); tbl3 <- bq_table_download(ds); bq_table_delete(ds)
tbl$psx - tbl3$psx
# Time difference of 0.0591259 secs
```

To support microsecond precision, 

```r
options(bigrquery.digits=22, bigrquery.digits.secs=6)
bq_table_upload(ds, tbl); tbl4 <- bq_table_download(ds); bq_table_delete(ds)
tbl$psx - tbl4$psx
# Time difference of 9.536743e-07 secs
```

Includes NEWS, code, and unit-tests.

title: fix 320, 660, and 661 (round-trip values relating to digits and tzone)
description:
A few facets, all related to round-trip handling of numbers and their precision.

Before this patch:

```r
bq_auth(path="my_token.json")
tbl <- data.frame(dbl=pi, psx=Sys.time())
ds <- bigrquery::bq_table(...)
bq_table_upload(ds, tbl); tbl2 <- bq_table_download(ds); bq_table_delete(ds)
tbl$psx - tbl2$psx
# Time difference of 5.000016 hours
```

The "5 hours" issue is due to missing the tzone on upload. By appending the timezone on uploaded `POSIXt` data, we get then

```r
bq_table_upload(ds, tbl); tbl3 <- bq_table_download(ds); bq_table_delete(ds)
tbl$psx - tbl3$psx
# Time difference of 0.0591259 secs
```

where 59 milliseconds can be an issue for those needing sub-second precision. (It crushes my work completely.)

Additionally,

```r
tbl$dbl - tbl2$dbl
# [1] 2.65359e-06
```

That's not as troublesome, but it has been discussed and requested that there be a mechanism to set the `digits=`/precision of uploaded data. After this patch:

```r
options(bigrquery.digits=22, bigrquery.digits.secs=6)
bq_table_upload(ds, tbl); tbl4 <- bq_table_download(ds); bq_table_delete(ds)
tbl$dbl - tbl4$dbl
# [1] 0
tbl$psx - tbl4$psx
# Time difference of 9.536743e-07 secs
```

title: Port all the underlying HTTP code to use httr2
description:
This commit refactors `bigrquery`'s internals to use `httr2` instead of `httr`. I don't have a strong motivation for this change, other than the general belief that we should be trying to move packages to `httr2` over time, and because it made `bigrquery`'s internals a bit more modular.

One of the more visible consequences is that the OAuth tokens returned by `bq_token()` can no longer take the form of an `httr` request object; now they are simple bearer tokens instead. This should make it much easier to implement viewer-based credentials in the future.

However, it might break downstream packages that rely on the existing `bq_token()` return value.

I believe that most of these changes should be covered by the existing test suite.

```r
}
```

title: Modify the bq_perform_query so that labels argument is respected
description:
Cost tracking is very important for BigQuery. This is done through labeling, but currently bigrquery does not support adding labels to the queries. 

This PR passess the ... argument to job configuration so if you add labels argument to the bq_project_query it is passed to BigQuery API and the job gets labeled

```
bq_project_query(bq_test_project(), "SELECT count(*) FROM publicdata.samples.natality", labels = list(test = test))
```

This query will get the label test with value test. 

I've tested internally and can confirm that this approach works. However this is a more of a proposal how to do that. Ideally either labels should be an argument which can be passed to all the high level functions, or there should be more clarity where argument ... is actually passed. 

Looking at the documentation for https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/jobs/insert which bq_perform_query posts to, the body should be a Job object, which is documented here https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job. Looking at that documentation the only setable argument is configuration, hence additional parameters should be passed there.

title: Download data in chunks that are more likely to be complete
description:
Fixes #412

The original bug is that some requests for `n` rows contain fewer than `n` rows, because the response gets truncated based on its size instead of its number of rows. This resulted in a returned data frame that smells OK: it has the right shape and first few hundreds or thousands of rows look fine, but they are then followed by empty rows (as many as necessary to deliver something with the user's requested number of rows).

High-level conclusions:

* We want to remain in charge of breaking the work into chunks, because then we can do downloads in parallel, which is totally worth it here. Letting Google paginate, then creeping through `pageToken`s is slow and also makes parsing + combining much more fiddly.
* We can't truly eliminate the possibility of server-side pagination, but now we actively check for it and throw an error if we've failed to retrieve all the requested rows.
* In the future, instead of engaging in more gymnastics around the awkward pagination behaviour of `bq_table_download()`, it's probably time to use the BigQuery Storage API.

Key links:

* API reference docs for `tabledata.list`: <https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/tabledata/list>
* Guide on "Paging through table data": <https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/paging-results>
* Related Python workflow: <https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/bigquery-storage-python-pandas>
* API docs for BigQuery Storage: <https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/storage>

**Issue:** Previously, `bq_table_download` would return empty rows in the returned data table when the temporary json files containing the data from BigQuery exceeded BigQuery's size limit (which seems to occur if a row contains an usually large amount of data like large amounts of text, large number arrays, or just a lot of fields). You could get around the problem by decreasing the page_size parameter, but since there was no indiction that this was occurring, debugging the issue took time and effort. See issues #311 and #412 for more details.

**Solution:** I have added a parameter to `bq_table_download` called `allow_fragments`. Additionally, I have added code that counts the number of total rows in the json files (num_observations) and compares this to the number of rows in the metadata of the BigQuery table (page_info$nrows).

If `allow_fragments = FALSE`, `bq_table_download` will throw an error if page_info$nrows != num_observations:

``` r
sql <- "SELECT * FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_wide` LIMIT 20000"
```

title: Add minimal support for GEOGRAPHY field type
description:
This is a PR to fix #388, and addresses issues identified with the previous PR (#376) that was closed.

The motivation is to make it possible for another package to wrap the [extensive BigQuery geography API](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/geography_functions), making use of the high-performance parsing and authentication management in this package. While it's possible to for a *user* to provide a workaround (e.g., using `ST_ASTEXT()`), it is difficult for a *package* to provide a workaround, since it doesn't know which (if any) columns contain geography that should be converted (very possible I'm missing an obvious workaround).

Options (as I see them) are:

- Continue to error on type GEOGRAPHY and make extension packages parse the JSON themselves if they want to support this column type (realistically, this would mean other packages would just copy `BqFields.cpp` and adapt for their own purposes)
- Return GEOGRAPHY as a character vector (this was the approach of #376)
- Return GEOGRAPHY as a character vector with a dummy class (this is the approach RPostgreSQL takes with unknown column types, where PostGIS columns are coerced to hex binary and given the class "pg_geometry")
- Return GEOGRAPHY as a [wk::wkt()](https://paleolimbot.github.io/wk/reference/wkt.html) vector, which is a thin wrapper around a character vector with a vctrs implementation (I maintain the wk package)
- Parse GEOGRAPHY into an [s2_geography vector](https://r-spatial.github.io/s2/reference/as_s2_geography.html), which uses the same C++ library as BigQuery geography (myself and @edzer maintain the s2 package)
- Parse GEOGRAPHY into an `sfc` from the sf package (maintained by  @edzer)

In this PR I took a middle-of-the-road approach with using `wk::wkt()`: the `wkt()` class doesn't do any parsing, but provides a recognizable class on which other packages can build without knowing anything about `bigrquery`. I'm happy to implement any of these, but I don't think continuing to error or returning a plain character vector is the way  to go.

I'm curious what @etiennebr and @edzer think about this, as they have practical experience with SQL and GIS that I don't.

title: Force BQ page query params to not use scientific notation
description:
Fixes #395.

I work on the All of Us Researcher Workbench project (https://github.com/all-of-us/workbench) where we guide users to fetch data from BigQuery via the bigrquery package. The issue above has been affecting our users, so we wanted to take a swing at a fix.

**Rationale**
This is a fix with more limited scope than the `httpr` alternative (https://github.com/r-lib/httr/pull/670). We simply force the page params 

**Testing**

- devtools::check() runs successfully.
- I confirmed that the added regression test fails if the code change is commented out.
- Open to suggestions for an alternative test strategy. This approach (using opts to force aggressive scientific formatting) is a bit more clever than I'd like, but it prevents us from needing to load ~100k rows to trigger this scenario.

**Notes**
An alternative to the approach in this PR would have been to use `as.integer(x)` instead of `format(x, scientific=FALSE)`. But that alternative relies on the implicit difference in R's formatting of integers vs. doubles, so I opted for the more explicit fix. I'd be curious to hear from reviewers if `as.integer` would be more robust or idiomatic.

title: Added db_save_query.bigquery so compute() now works
description:
Hello everyone! This pull request features an implementation of `db_save_query` for "bigquery". This is my first attempt to contribute to `bigrquery` project so I apologize in advance if I am missing some key details (or may be even being overly verbose in describing it)

_NOTE_: had to resubmit pull request since had to move it from master to a separate branch in my repository. (The original pull request is #51 .)
### Motivation

The motivation for this pull request is that the current implementation of `bigrquery` allows one to use `collect` function (that is, saving the results locally) but not `compute` function (that is, saving the results remotely).

`Compute` function seems to be extremely important when working with big datasets as it allows one to keep big temporary remotely results in Google BigQuery without downloading them locally and use them in subsequent queries.
### Implementation Details
- `compute` function fails only because of the lack of `db_save_query.bigquery`.
  Fortunately, `query_exec` facilities allow saving the query result and thus, `db_save_query` could potentially be implemented as a hook to query_exec with a particular `destination_table`.
- `temporary = TRUE` is not currently implemented and is currently ignored so all tables are created as persistent.
### Tests

The code belows demonstrates a simple test of `compute` function. 

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(bigrquery)

BILLING_PROJECT <- "<YOUR_BILLING_PROJECT>"
BILLING_DATASET <- "<DATASET_INSIDE_THAT_PROJECT>"

bq <- src_bigquery(BILLING_PROJECT, BILLING_DATASET)

# Upload the test data frame to your project
df <- data.frame(a = 1:100, b = 101:200)
test_df <- copy_to(bq, df, name = "test_df")

# Perform a simple query and save the result remotely
test_df2 <- test_df %>%
              summarise( n = n() ) %>%
```

title: Implemented sql_join for Google BigQuery
description:
Hello everyone! This pull request features an implementation of `sql_join` for "bigquery".

(I apologize for shuffling this pull request between two repositories: it used to be in hadley/dplyr#1224 but I figured out from hadley/dplyr#434 that all BigQuery-related things are supposed to go to `bigrquery` package instead.) 
### Motivation

The major motivation for this pull request is that Google BigQuery has powerful SQL join facilities but requires a particular dialect of SQL when doing joins such that regular `sql_join` fails to produce a runnable query.
- Example: SQL keyword "USING" is not supported and the complete column name specification is required. (The default `sql_join.DBIConnection` solution when joining two tables A and B on the common column id is to say  "A JOIN B USING id" while Google BigQuery requires to say "A JOIN B on A.id = B.id")
- Example: Subsequently, Google Query is very sensitive to ambigous names inside SELECT statement and would require one to specify SELECT A.id or SELECT B.id instead of SELECT id which required some change in the logic of `sql_join`.
- Example: When joining large tables "JOIN EACH" keyword is required instead of "JOIN"
### Implementation Details

Some points that are probably worth clarifying for this pull request:
- _`sql_subquery.bigquery` is modified_. The problem with the current version `sql_subquery.bigquery` is that `dplyr::build_sql` erases "vars" attribute when creating a subquery. However, "vars" are needed for correct subsequent processing of the join. I decided to go with the smallest and safest change possible and just added back "vars" to SQL object.
- only `collect()` works and not `compute()` would work with this pull request. (`compute()` fails due to missing `db_save_query.bigquery` which I submitted as a separate pull request here #52 )
- the function is compatible (and tested) with future `cross_join` that is planned to be implemented as in hadley/dplyr#197 
### Tests

The code belows demonstrates a test of BigQuery JOIN via dplyr using publicly available data on Google Cloud. Please note that running the test does require to have a Google Cloud billing project set up already. 

The test should run for several seconds and billed for ~9GB of data (~$0.05 USD)

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(bigrquery)

shakespeare <- 
   src_bigquery("publicdata", "samples", billing="<BILLING_PROJECT>") %>% 
   tbl("shakespeare")
wikipedia <- 
   src_bigquery("publicdata", "samples", billing="<BILLING_PROJECT>") %>% 
   tbl("wikipedia")

result <-
  shakespeare %>% 
  select(word, word_count) %>%
  inner_join(wikipedia %>% select(title, num_characters),
             by=c("word"="title")) %>% 
  summarise( n = n(),
             word_count = sum(word_count),
             num_characters = max(num_characters)) %>%
  collect

result
```

Thanks for consideration!

title: mutate_ always requires collapsing in BigQuery
description:
This pull request fixes the issue with `mutate` in BigQuery when the variables created with `mutate` cannot be used in subsequent operators (as explained below).
### Motivation

BigQuery does not allow one to use column alias in the same query where it is assigned as explained [in the reference](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/query-reference#select), and therefore, the variable created by `mutate_` cannot be used until one collapses the SQL query first.

Knowing this, it may be beneficial in Google BigQuery to collapse the query immediately after mutate so that the very next operator can use the newly created variable.
### Tests

The code belows demonstrates the failure of regular `mutate_`

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(bigrquery)

BILLING_PROJECT <- "<YOUR_BILLING_PROJECT>"
BILLING_DATASET <- "<DATASET_INSIDE_THAT_PROJECT>"

bq <- src_bigquery(BILLING_PROJECT, BILLING_DATASET)

# Upload the test data frame to your project
df <- data.frame(a = 1:100, b = 101:200)

mutate_df <- copy_to(bq, df, name = "mutate_df")

# Perform two consecutive mutate queries 
# where 2nd mutate uses the variable created in the 1st mutate
mutate_df %>%
  mutate( c = a + 1 ) %>%
  mutate( d = c + 1 ) %>% 
  explain
```

This produces the following query

``` sql
SELECT [a], [b], [a] + 1.0 AS [c], [c] + 1.0 AS [d]
FROM [mutate_df]
```

which is not allowed in BigQuery as per [reference](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/query-reference#select) and will return an error:

```
Error: Field 'c' not found in table 'mutate_df'; did you mean 'a'?

query invalidQuery. Field 'c' not found in table 'mutate_df'; did you mean 'a'?
```
### Contribution

This pull request makes sure to collapse the query once mutate is used. This allows one to use the newly created names in the subsequent operators. With pull request, the same code as before:

``` r
mutate_df %>%
  mutate( c = a + 1 ) %>%
  mutate( d = c + 1 ) %>% 
  explain
```

produces

``` sql
SELECT [a], [b], [c], [d]
FROM (SELECT [a], [b], [c], [c] + 1.0 AS [d]
FROM (SELECT [a], [b], [a] + 1.0 AS [c]
FROM [mutate_df]) AS [_W1]) AS [_W2]
```

which is now a legitimate BigQuery query that produces the correct answer.

Thank you for consideration!

The motivation for this pull request is that the current implementation of `bigrquery` allows one to use `collect` function (that is, saving the results locally) but not `compute` function (that is, saving the results remotely).

`Compute` function seems to be extremely important when working with big datasets as it allows one to keep big temporary remotely results in Google BigQuery without downloading them locally and use them in subsequent queries.

  Fortunately, `query_exec` facilities allow saving the query result and thus, `db_save_query` could potentially be implemented as a hook to query_exec with a particular `destination_table`.
- `temporary = TRUE` is not currently implemented and is currently ignored so all tables are created as persistent.
- This pull request works correctly with the suggested `dplyr` pull request [hadley/dplyr#1220](https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/pull/1220) which also implements JOINs inside BigQuery. Together these two pull requests can extend the current functionality to allow both JOINing remotely and storing the results remotely.

title: non-stop runing
description:
When querying from the BIgQuery and using where clause, if BigQuery direct web access (https://bigquery.cloud.google.com/) returns "Query returned zero records" with seconds, the same query using this package won't stop and return any results; but if  BigQuery direct web access returns table results, the same query running perfect in bigrquery.

Any reason for this? Thanks a lot.

title: Add an additional scope for BQ credentials.
description:
This is one of the "standard" scopes in the BQ API description; it's not
strictly required for anything right now, but no reason not to include it.

Also fixed a typo.

title: Added support for data type timestamp in BigQuery
description:
As I got the error: Don't know how to convert type timestamp, timestamp was not supported.
Based on the description of BigQuery, Timestamp is "A decimal number specifying the number of seconds since the epoch." which is a time since 1970-01-01, the conversion function added in the code.

title: Add a regression test for nested proto/struct extraction
description: This is expected to fail now due to the regression in {dbplyr} (tidyverse/dbplyr#1881), but filing this PR so that when the fix upstream lands, we get a signal of any future breakage here.
